cells.tense: The joining is underway right now and your hands are in it.
cells.ask: Offer the growing thing one more day of your steady attention than you'd planned, and let the ease of it feed what you start next.
cells.core: You're tending what's coming up, and it has your whole attention. Good days here look like a morning at the bench with your hands in something already underway without you — you add the water and step back, and it keeps going. The direction comes out of being genuinely in it, not out of resolve laid over the top.\n\nWhat's gathered in you now is momentum you didn't have to force. The next thing you choose to feed gets that same steadiness, and it doesn't cost you anything to give it. That's the move — the joining is already carrying you, so the ask is only to trust it one more step.
cells.sheetLine: You're in the middle of it and it's holding.
cells.verb: choosing one stream and letting it carry you into a single flow
cells.place: in the care of what is growing

cells.tense: You're already living past this moment, bracing for what hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Set down one thing you've been holding for the future and let it ripen by the fact of your having tended it — then enjoy what's already grown without planning the next crop.
cells.core: When this is steady, you're in the garden at the hour it actually is, watering what's in front of you and not the bed you'll plant next spring. The bench is where you sit down, the work is the work you can touch, and the growing happens at its own speed without you standing over it. Nothing urgent is missing. You know what today's tending is because you can see the plant.\n\nThen it tips. You're carrying this growing thing further ahead than it actually is. You've rehearsed the outcome, then the outcome after that, and your hands are still moving over work that's already done growing. Care at this pitch doesn't produce anything faster — it just makes you tired of something that was never asking that much from you. Put one thing down in the middle of its own ripening, and let enjoyment be the whole of your part today.
cells.sheetLine: You're ahead of the growing thing instead of with it.
cells.verb: choosing one stream and letting it carry you into a single flow
cells.place: in the care of what is growing

cells.tense: You're still standing at a joining that's already happened, and you haven't walked through it.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you plainly see about what's growing in front of you, and let the accuracy of it stand without defending it.
cells.core: There's care you mean to give, and it hasn't arrived. You stand back from what's coming up as if getting close to it were the risk — so the tending happens at a distance, or doesn't happen at all, and the thing grows with nobody's hands actually on it. What's missing isn't the wish to care. It's walking over and doing it.\n\nDone plainly, it looks like this: you cross the room, you see what the plant needs, you do it without a moment of argument with yourself. That plainness is yours already, and it isn't in question. Give it to one person today, in one sentence about what you actually see.
cells.sheetLine: The care is there, but your hands haven't shown up.
cells.verb: choosing one stream and letting it carry you into a single flow
cells.place: in the care of what is growing

cells.tense: The joining is already running — you're just calling it something other than you.
cells.ask: Point at one thing you've been treating as just how things are and say, in words, that you're the one who put it there.
cells.core: You're already joined to what's growing — the way you notice what needs water, the way you talk about the plant as if it belonged to no one. That's you doing it. But when you say it out loud, you say the thing grew on its own, or the season did it, and your part drops out of the story.\n\nDone well, this looks like a garden where someone's hand is visible — the stake you placed, the pruning you chose, the direction you quietly set. The care was never absent; the saying-so is what's been missing. Name one thing you did and hand it back to yourself, today, once.
cells.sheetLine: You set the direction. You've been calling it the season.
